transcript: Kiva read it at the back of the crowd, with Prue beside her and Perrin behind, under the lamp, while the tide went out of the timber pond's black water under the boards. Every one of the twelve lanes had gone to the four that stood higher. The tarn's first four had stood with Truen, on frosted feet and a reserve at Bridie's place, and had won by a single point than the glass. Haldin License had beaten the twenty-fourth six to two. The rope walks seven to nothing stood at the head of the column, alone. Team seven-nine beat the tarn, second four sixteen, seven to two. Seven, said Perrin, with no fingers.
